Speaker's Card/Request to Speak:
If you would like to address the City Council/Agency on a scheduled agenda item - including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments - please complete the Request to Speak Form . The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The Request to Speak Form assists the Mayor/Chair in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council/Agency are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council/Agency. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor/Chair), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.

ADJOURNMENT-CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council and Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council and/or Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council/Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council/Successor Agency. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Successor Agency Board at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council/Successor Agency are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

 City Council Minutes  January 14, 2020

  MOMENT OF SILENCE

  Mayor Shea asked for a moment of silence in memory of the 176 people who died in the
  Ukrainian plane crash on January 8.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Lee Yi from Saddleback Church in Irvine provided the invocation.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Proclaim January 13, 2020 as "Korean American Day"

  Mayor Shea introduced the following individuals and presented a
  proclamation recognizing January 13, 2020 as “Korean American Day”:

  •  Juweon Yun, President, Orange County Korean Cultural Center and
  his wife Grace
  •  Diane Kim, OC Korean Cultural Center
  •  Esther Koh, on behalf of Assemblyman Steven Choi
  •  Juneu Kim, President, Irvine Korean Evergreen Association
  •  Tammy Kim, Korean American Center
  •  Migyung Lee, King Sejong Institute
  •  Lawrence Lim and Naki Park, Reporters, Korea Daily

  2.2  Proclaim January 20, 2020 as "Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day"

  Mayor Shea introduced Bobby MacDonald, President and CEO, Black
  Chamber of Commerce of Orange County, and presented a proclamation
  recognizing January 20, 2020 as “Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day.”

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  •  City Manager Russo, on behalf of the City Council, announced that the City of Irvine
  had reached an agreement in general with Wild Rivers Irvine, LLC with respect to
  price and terms for the construction of a water park at the Orange County Great
  Park, and anticipates having the agreement before the Orange County Great Park
  Board and City Council on February 25.

  •  Chief Hamel noted a recently executed Memorandum of Understanding between
  the cities of Irvine, Laguna Beach, and Newport Beach that would enhance the City
  of Irvine’s ability to respond and recover from wild land fires and other natural
  disasters.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  January 14, 2020

  •  Kristin Griffith, Director of Financial Management and Strategic Planning, provided
  an update on the Fiscal Year 2018-19 General Fund Year-End report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  •  Councilmember Carroll provided background and other information on the recently
  established Ad Hoc Safe Community Task Force Meeting, and announced an
  upcoming meeting scheduled on February 4, 2020.

  •  Councilmember Khan announced an upcoming town hall meeting that she will be
  hosting on Friday, January 31, 2020 at 4 p.m. in light of recent events and concerns
  raised by the Iranian community. Additional information will be forthcoming.

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  The City of Irvine is installing a new traffic control device to help make crossing
  busy streets easier for pedestrians. The first device has been activated on Alton
  Parkway adjacent to the Edwards Lifesciences Corporate Campus. The new
  device, called a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon, or PHB, provides safety enhancements
  to crosswalks, especially in mid-block locations that are heavily traveled by
  pedestrians. Drivers experience minimal delays as the devices are only activated
  when a pedestrian is present. PHBs have been used in various agencies throughout
  the country to improve service for pedestrians. For information, visit cityofirvine.org.

  •  Since fire season began in September, more than 14 million acres have been
  scorched in Australia, roughly the size of West Virginia. At least 26 people have
  died, 2,000 homes have been destroyed, and approximately one billion animals
  have been killed.

  3.3  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 20-01 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING

  FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID

  3.4  SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 19-19 TO AMEND
  CHAPTERS 9-1, 9-6, 9-9, AND 9-40 OF THE ZONING ORDINANCE
  RELATED TO THE TRANSFER OF UNBUILT RESIDENTIAL
  DWELLING UNITS FROM PLANNING AREAS 9 (WOODBURY) AND 40
  (CYPRESS VILLAGE) TO PLANNING AREAS 1 (ORCHARD HILLS)
  AND 6 (PORTOLA SPRINGS)

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of Jeff
  Davis, the Irvine Company, who spoke in support of the revised
  ordinance, and noted a written request by the Irvine Company to
  eliminate any reference to Portola Springs in the proposed ordinance.

  Ali Kakar, Irvine resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed ordinance.

  City Council discussion included: providing a chronology and history
  related to the approval of the first reading of the ordinance; noted
  compliance with the City’s General Plan; referenced concerns raised by
  nearby residents regarding intensity and impacts to schools; noted the

  5.2  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR SHEA AND MAYOR PRO
  TEMPORE CARROLL TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION OPPOSING THE
  MODIFIED REGIONAL HOUSING NEEDS ASSESSMENT ALLOCATION
  METHODOLOGY

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Shea and Mayor Pro
  Tempore Carroll, who asked for City Council consideration to adopt a
  resolution opposing the modified Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  (RHNA) allocation methodology.

  Marika Poynter, Principal Planner, responded to City Council questions.
  Kerwin Lau, Manager of Planning Services, was also available for questions.

  Susan Sayre, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the proposed resolution,
  expressing concern about the modified allocation.

  City Council discussion included: expressing concern about the current
  methodology for allocating units; questioned where the approximate 22,000
  units would be built; inquired about the allocation of units during the previous
  two cycles and how many of those units were built; questioned whether
  punitive damages would ensue; reiterated that the proposed resolution was
  more focused on the process/methodology as opposed to the modified
  number of units; inquired about the legal intention of the proposed resolution;
  expressed concern related to increases in traffic; and noted that the 5,000
  unit cap had been reached in the Irvine Business Complex.

  City Manager Russo noted that staff would reach out to other nearby cities
  to reiterate the City of Irvine’s opposition to the modified allocation of units.

  The following individuals submitted a request to speak but did not speak:

  Nicholas Bull, Irvine resident
  Nicholas DeNuccio, Irvine resident
  Chris Youde, Cosmetic Fog Vapors Manufacturing
  Katheryn, Irvine resident
  Jeffrey Nelson, Irvine resident
  Shaun Providence, Streamline
  George Jonson, Hookah Chamber of Commerce

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether the proposed
  ordinance was applicable to hookah use; inquired about the age of statistical
  information provided in the staff report; expressed concern about how the
  products are marketed to children; suggested shifting enforcement to those
  selling the product; inquired about concerns raised by the American Lung
  Association; suggested collaboration with Irvine schools to address the
  problem; inquired about the legal age to acquire tobacco products;
  questioned enforcement for retailers who sell to those who are underage;
  suggested that staff return to the City Council with sales of flavored tobacco
  products in the City, including how much revenue is generated, and a
  method to audit retailers to allow inspections; and suggested a study of other
  enforcement mechanisms.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that language in the ordinance could be
  amended to 1) exclude hookah as a prohibited use, and 2) be limited to
  enforcement to minors; and 3) remove the provision that prohibits retailers
  from selling flavored tobacco products.
